== Biography ==
Robert Glasgow was baptised at Irvine, Ayrshire, on 10 January 1716, a son of John Glasgow and Isabell Kyle.<ref name="birth1716">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573222&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/3573222], OPR 595/1, transcript of the baptism on 10 January 1716 naming John Glasgow and Isabell Kyle as parents; captured 3 September 2026. Also "Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTV2-YVQ Robert Glasgow, 1716], accessed 27 September 2026).</ref>

Robert Glasgow and Mary Borland were named as the parents of a John Glasgow baptised at Irvine on 10 October 1736. Another John Glasgow, [[Glasgow-3478]], was baptised there on 5 October 1738 with the same named parents.<ref name="john1736">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Irvine Old Parish Registers, OPR 595/1, transcript of John Glasgow's baptism on 10 October 1736, naming Robt Glasgow and Mary Borland; captured 3 September 2026. See the detailed citation on [[Glasgow-3478]].</ref><ref name="john1738">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', SCOT/OPR/BAP/3574782, OPR 595/1, John Glasgow baptised 5 October 1738, father Rot Glasgow and mother Mary Borland; captured 3 September 2026. MyHeritage, ''Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950'', film 1041383, [https://www.myheritage.com/research/record-30226-305754/john-glasgow-in-scotland-births-baptisms John Glasgow entry], also gives 5 October 1738 and these parents. The transcripts disagree on John's birth month; see [[Glasgow-3478]].</ref>

An Irvine burgh catalogue entry dated 4 August 1738 names Robert Glasgow as master of the ship ''Betty and Grizell'' of Irvine. His name, town and date fit the father in the baptism records, although the catalogue entry itself does not identify his family.<ref name="ship1738">Ayrshire Archives, ''Irvine Burgh Catalogue'' (2017), IB2/14/71, p. 148, 4 August 1738, [https://web.archive.org/web/20190919232657/https://ayrshirearchives.files.wordpress.com/2019/04/irvine-burgh-catalogue-2017-watermarked.pdf archived catalogue]. The entry describes the sale of an eighth share in the ship ''Betty and Grizell'' of Irvine, with Robert Glasgow as master, and notes an inventory. The underlying sale and inventory have not been inspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Additional parish and later-life evidence ===
Robert Glasgow baptised 16 November 1740 at Ayr, Robert Glasgow and Mary Borland. John Glasgow-3478 has a similarly named parental couple (Glasgow-2474 and Borland-1479) in an Irvine context, but no family bridge establishes these adults or a sibling relationship. Retain a qualified named-father comparison; no child creation or attachment. Inspected Findmypast derivative; original register or memorial uninspected. No new person, attachment or relationship-confidence change.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2475]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Robert’s 10 January 1716 Irvine baptism names John Glasgow and Isabell Kyle, matching the full couple and sequence of the selected John’s household.

Confident for this recorded child and parental couple; spelling variation is retained.

Next useful test: Check the original entry if the Kyle/Keil reading matters to maternal research.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573222&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3573222 (), OPR 595/1, transcript of the baptism on 10 January 1716 naming John Glasgow and Isabell Kyle as parents; captured 3 September 2026]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


The 1716 Irvine baptism and the 1736–1738 Irvine household are treated as one person. Robert would have been about twenty when the first John was baptised and twenty-two at the 1738 ship entry. The later records do not name Robert's parents, so the identification is an evidence-based inference rather than a direct statement in a single record. No conflicting event or stronger same-name candidate has been found. The former separate adult profile [[Glasgow-3479]] was merged into this baptism profile on 27 September 2026; its estimated birth about 1720 or before 1719 was based on adult chronology, not a separate birth record.

The 1736 and 1738 John baptism entries may describe two sons of the same name, with the elder dying young, or an index or register discrepancy. The 1736 entry was formerly represented by [[Glasgow-4118]], which now redirects to [[Glasgow-3478]]. The original register images need comparison before deciding whether these entries concern one or two children. The attached [[Glasgow-3478]] includes the 1738 baptism.

The shipmaster identification is likewise likely on locality and chronology, but the catalogue does not itself connect the master to Mary Borland or to Robert's parents. Inspect IB2/14/71 and related Irvine records for a family-identifying bridge.

=== Possible Captain Glasgow, brig Ann and Larne passenger reports, 1788 ===
The brig Ann is listed inward with Glasgow as master and Larne as origin.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/604128637/ The Columbian Herald, or, The Independent Courier of North-America, 1788-01-28, p.2].</ref>

The brig Ann, Captain Glasgow, is reported arriving from Larne after a tedious passage with near 200 passengers in good health; the report praises the captain’s humane and generous behaviour.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1034014648/ The Pennsylvania Journal, or, Weekly Advertiser, 1788-02-13, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39957255/ The Independent Gazetteer, 1788-02-16, p.2].</ref>

The brig Ann is listed cleared out with Glasgow as master and Georgetown as destination.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/604128661/ The Columbian Herald, or, The Independent Courier of North-America, 1788-02-18, p.2].</ref>

The passenger reports repeat one notice. The inward and outward entries may concern the same captain, but none gives his forename or family; Larne is the voyage origin, not a recorded birthplace.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2474]]. Robert born 1716 would be about 72. Prior public research reports a 1738 Irvine shipmaster; no connection to Ann or Larne.

=== Possible Captain Glasgow, vessel William at New-York, 1758 ===
A February 1758 shipping report lists the vessel William, master Glasgow, from London, at New-York.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/34419759/ The Public Advertiser, 1758-02-18, p.1].</ref>

William is the vessel’s name; the master’s personal forename is not stated. The voyage does not identify his residence, birthplace or family.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2474]]. Recorded 1716 Irvine birth and prior 1738 shipmaster study make a compatible occupational candidate. This 1758 notice supplies no personal forename or vessel identification.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, master of John and Archibald, 1754 ===
Robert Glasgow, master of the snow John and Archibald, of Glasgow, is reported arriving in distress during a Virginia-to-Glasgow passage.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39398244/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1754-03-19, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971274921/ The Gloucester Journal, 1754-06-25, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1212017118/ Berrow’s Worcester Journal, 1754-06-27, p.1].</ref>

These are reprints of one shipping report. "Of Glasgow" describes the vessel; John and Archibald is its name, not two relatives of the master.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2474]]. The occupational comparison is relevant: age 38 and the 1738 shipmaster record is relevant prior maritime evidence. No direct connection to Snow John and Archibald. A Findmypast baptism transcript records him at Irvine. The cited accounts associate the adult Robert Glasgow-3479 with Irvine family entries and report an Irvine Burgh Catalogue entry (4 Aug 1738) naming Robert Glasgow master of the Irvine ship Betty and Grizell; the family identification remains qualified.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, Old Bailey and Newgate reports, 1751 ===
Robert Glasgow is reported among nine Old Bailey convicts receiving judgment of death, for highway robbery of Joseph Weedon’s gold ring, silver shoe buckles and other things.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971486582/ The Gloucester Journal, 1751-07-16, p.2].</ref>

Robert Glasgow, condemned for robbing Joseph Weedon on the highway, is included among Newgate prisoners ordered for execution on Monday next.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979343886/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury, 1751-07-29, p.2].</ref>

The judgment and later order for execution are separate reports. An order for execution is not proof that it occurred; neither report supplies the relatives or origin needed to identify Robert among the Scottish namesakes.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2474]]. Possible; age 35, no concrete chronology conflict. The newspaper’s later execution order is a serious unresolved continuity issue, but execution itself is not established. A Findmypast baptism transcript records him at Irvine. The cited accounts associate the adult Robert Glasgow-3479 with Irvine family entries and report an Irvine Burgh Catalogue entry (4 Aug 1738) naming Robert Glasgow master of the Irvine ship Betty and Grizell; the family identification remains qualified.
